title: Hungnam evacuation, December 1950
summary: After General MacArthur decided to withdraw, US X Corps left northeast Korea by sea from Hungnam between 9 and 24 December 1950, taking out over 100,000 troops with their supplies. About 98,100 Korean refugees were also evacuated from Hungnam, Wonsan and Songjin, while a similar number were left behind for lack of ship space. The port was destroyed on departure.

as_recorded.value: On Dec. 9, 1950, the first evacuations began ... Continuing through Dec. 24
The Refugee Evacuation from Hungnam: 9-24 December 1950

where.modern_name: Hungnam, Hamhung, South Hamgyong Province, North Korea
where.historical_name: Hungnam, North Korea (then held by UN forces; port of the Hamhung-Hungnam area)

importance.justification: One of the largest sea evacuations of the 20th century, ending the UN advance into North Korea and shaping Korean refugee migration southward.

beats.caption: Mass evacuation of troops, supplies and refugees from Hungnam began on 9 December.
The last X Corps units sailed on Christmas Eve and the port was destroyed.
About 98,100 refugees left from Hungnam, Wonsan and Songjin; an equal number were left behind for lack of space.

reviewer_note: Refugee figures vary by source (98,100 on the DVIDS page; navy-only counts are lower) and the counter uses the DVIDS figure. 'Over 100,000 troops' is from the DVIDS quote of a US Army history and the ARSOF article's reference to planning for 100,000 troops. The pin is Hungnam's Wikidata point.
